rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naʿīm covers every blessing that gives pleasure, including life, health, well-being, and even a sip of sweet cold water.
rows.anchor: “Na‘îm” kendisiyle telezzüz olunan her türlü nimete şâmildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, the warning addresses people distracted by rivalry; the blessing meant is what heedless enjoyment uses to divert them from religion and its duties.
rows.anchor: hitab tekâsür kendilerini lehv ile oyalamış olanlara, o na‘îmden murad da öyle lehv ü gafletle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the narrower contextual reading, questioning means reproachfully reminding people of blessings they have lost and making them suffer their pain and punishment.
rows.anchor: onların acılarını, azablarını çektirmektir.

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari identifies the questioned blessings as those of people who spend all their effort on pleasures, fine food and clothing, and amusement while neglecting knowledge and deeds.
rows.anchor: Onun için Keşşâf’ta der ki: “‘İnsanın mes’ul ve mu‘âteb olacağı na‘îm nedir? Çünkü hiç nimeti olmayan kimse yoktur?’ dersen, derim ki: O bütün himmeti

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: Those who use God-given provisions to gain knowledge, do good deeds, and give thanks are exempt from this blameworthy questioning.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf’ın da ihtar[^24] eylediği vechile şükredenlerin bu sualden âzâde olacaklarına

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: A report about the Prophet and Companions eating dates and drinking water, then praising God, illustrates the thankful use of blessings.
rows.anchor: Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Hazretleri rivayet olunduğu üzere ashâbıyla bir hurma yiyip üzerine su içtiklerinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, both unbelievers wholly heedless of religion and sinful believers heedless of religious obligations are questioned, while righteous, thankful believers are not.
rows.anchor: Bunda dinden büsbütün gaflet eden kâfirler dâhil olduğu gibi tekâlîf-i dîniyeden gaflet eden fâsık mü’minler de dâhil olur.

rows.speaker: Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi glosses the blessing as what distracts the addressee from religion and limits the immediate address to anyone whose worldly life distracts them from religion.
rows.anchor: Beyzâvî bunu şöyle hulâsa etmiştir: “‘Na‘îm’, yani o sizi ilhâ eden na‘îm demektir.

rows.speaker: Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi says contextual indications, including Qurʾān 7:32, support restricting the intended blessing to what distracts from religion.
rows.anchor: Beyzâvî bunu şöyle hulâsa etmiştir: “‘Na‘îm’, yani o sizi ilhâ eden na‘îm demektir. Hitab, dünyası dininden ilhâ eyleyen her kimseye, na‘îm de onu işgal eyleyene

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi also notes broader positions: both address and blessing may be general, everyone may be questioned about gratitude, or the verse may concern unbelievers alone.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh ikisi de âmdır. ‘Herkes şükründen mes’ul olacaktır’ da denilmiş, ‘âyet küffâra mahsustur’ da denilmiş.

rows.speaker: Hasan, Mukātil ve İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Some exegetes, transmitting views from Hasan, Muqatil, and Ibn Abbas, hold that the surah addresses unbelievers and this question is their recompense-question.
rows.anchor: Hasan ve Mukātil’den ve İbn Abbas’tan mervî olarak bazı müfessirîn bu sûredeki hitapların kâfirlere

rows.speaker: Hasan, Mukātil ve İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Those exegetes cite Qurʾān 34:17 as evidence that recompense is directed to the ungrateful unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وَهَلْ نُجَٰزِىٓ إِلَّا ٱلْكَفُورَ [es-Sebe’ 34/17] buyurulmuş olmasıyla da istidlâl eylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If kufr here means ingratitude for a blessing, the unbeliever-specific interpretation amounts to the preceding interpretation of heedless, ungrateful use.
rows.anchor: Fakat bundan murad küfrân-ı nimet olduğuna göre evvelki mânaya müsâvî olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other exegetes take the address to include all people and naʿīm to mean every kind of blessing; questioning discloses ingratitude or gratitude and leads to punishment or reward.
rows.anchor: Diğer bir kısım müfessirîn de sûrenin

rows.speaker: Zübeyr b. Avvam
rows.claim: When the verse was revealed, Zubayr asked which blessings would be questioned, naming dates and water; the Prophet answered that this would indeed happen.
rows.anchor: Zübeyr b. Avvam radıyallâhu anh: “Yâ Resûlallah, biz hangi na‘îmden sual olunacağız

rows.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
rows.claim: In another report, people ask which blessing they will face while they have only dates and water, with an enemy present and swords at their necks; the Prophet says it will happen.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hüreyre’den rivayette: “Nâs yâ Resûlallah! Biz hangi na‘îmden sual olunacağız?

rows.speaker: Tirmizî
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the Zubayr report hasan and the other report more sound.
rows.anchor: Tirmizî evvelkine hasen ve ikinciden esah demiştir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says the first questioning about a servant’s blessings will ask whether God gave bodily health and quenched thirst with cold water; al-Tirmidhi calls it gharīb.
rows.anchor: Yine Ebû Hüreyre’den; Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem buyurmuştur ki

rows.speaker: Ömer
rows.claim: Umar asks about questioning after the Muslims were driven from their homeland and wealth; the Prophet names homes, shade, and cold water as blessings.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer’den rivayet olunmuştur; “hangi na‘îmden sorulacağız yâ Resûlallah! Hâlbuki diyarımızdan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A related prophetic saying treats safety at home, bodily health, and a day’s food as equivalent to possessing the whole world.
rows.anchor: bedeni âfiyette, gününün azığı yanında olan kimse sanki dünya tamamıyla ona

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A newly converted young man refused his bride’s abundant dowry and household blessings, saying he could not answer for them when the Prophet had taught him this verse.
rows.anchor: Bir de Resûlullah zamanında bir genç Müslüman olmuştu, Resûlullah ona أَلْهَىٰكُمُ ٱلتَّكَاثُرُ sûresini öğretmişti

rows.speaker: Enes
rows.claim: Anas reports that a needy man asked whether he had any blessing, and the Prophet named shade, two sandals, and cold water.
rows.anchor: Ve Enes’ten mervîdir ki: “Bu âyet nâzil olduğu zaman bir muhtaç kalkmış

rows.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra narrates that the hungry Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar were welcomed by an Ansari, ate dates and sheep, and drank; the Prophet swore they would be questioned about that meal.
rows.anchor: Müslim, Ebû Dâvûd, Tirmizî, Nesâî, İbn Mâce ve daha diğerlerinin Ebû Hüreyre’den rivayet ettikleri şu hadistir

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s report, the Prophet and companions ate dates and goat at Abu Ayyub’s home, sent food to Fatima, and the Prophet identified the meal as a blessing about which they would be questioned.
rows.anchor: İbn Hibbân’ın ve İbn Merdûye’nin İbn Abbas’tan rivayetlerinde

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: After the meal, the Prophet told the companions to say bismillah when eating and praise God after eating, saying this would suffice for that blessing.
rows.anchor: Böylesine isabet edip de el sürdüğünüz vakit بِسْمِ الله deyin, doyduğunuz vakit de الْحَمْدُ للهِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports support universal questioning, though the final report, as al-Zamakhshari notes, indicates that the thankful are spared it.
rows.anchor: şükredenlerin bu sualden âzâde olacaklarına delâlet etmektedir.

rows.speaker: İmâm Râzî
rows.claim: Al-Razi argues that questioning includes believers and unbelievers and both necessary and non-necessary blessings, because every divine gift must be used in obedience rather than disobedience.
rows.anchor: Fakat İmâm Râzî Tefsîr-i Kebîr’inde demiştir ki: “Elhak sual nimetlerin, gerek lâbüd olanlar

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A prophetic report says a servant’s feet will not move on Judgment Day until questioned about lifespan, youth, wealth and its use, and knowledge and its use; al-Razi says these encompass all blessings.
rows.anchor: Bunu rivayet olunan şu hadîs-i nebevî de tekid eyler: ‘Kıyamet günü, dört şeyden sual olunmadıkça

rows.speaker: İmâm Râzî
rows.claim: Al-Razi distinguishes the unbeliever’s question as reproach for abandoning gratitude and the believer’s question as an honor for gratitude and obedience.
rows.anchor: Bununla beraber Râzî şunu da ihtar eylemiştir: “Lâkin kâfire olan sual tevbih suâlidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author defines accountability as consequences for whether every blessing is used properly: wrong use brings punishment, while fulfilling one’s duty brings reward.
rows.anchor: Burada mes’ûliyetin mânası her nimetin sû’-i isti‘mâline, mahalline sarfolunup olunmadığına göre sevab veya ikāb terettüb etmesi mânasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every accountable person is liable, and the greater the blessings, the greater and heavier the duties and accountability; this explains the focus on distracting rivalry.
rows.anchor: nimet ne kadar çok olursa vazifesi de o nisbette çok ve zor, mes’ûliyeti de o nisbette büyük ve ağır olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and Companions avoided rivalry by living alongside the poorest members of the community.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah ve ashâbı maîşetlerinde ümmetin en fakirleriyle hemhâl olarak tekâsürden son derece ihtiraz buyurmuşlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and Abu Bakr were not poor by compulsion; they chose poverty through generosity and patience, spending their means on the community, in keeping with the counsel to spend moderately.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber ve Hazret-i Ebû Bekir fakr-ı ıztırârî ile fakir değillerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because accountability is inherent in obligation, it cannot be restricted to unbelievers; Qurʾān 17:29 counsels moderation in this context.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde mükellefiyetin bir lâzımı demek olan mes’ûliyet yalnız kâfirlere mahsus olamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾān 2:173 removes blame in necessity, so necessities are exempt from questioning and reckoning to the extent required; a report likewise exempts shade, a bread crust, and clothing covering nakedness.
rows.anchor: Evvelâ; فَمَنِ ٱضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍۢ وَلَا عَادٍۢ فَلَآ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ [el-Bakara 2/173] mûcebince zarûret hâllerinde

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: A report attributed to Hasan says servants are not reckoned for a hut’s shade, a morsel that strengthens the back, or a garment that covers nakedness, challenging al-Razi’s universal scope over necessities.
rows.anchor: Abdullah b. İmam Ahmed’in ve Deylemî’nin Hasan’dan tahric eyledikleri şu hadis de buna delâlet eyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi’s unrestricted generalization even to indispensable necessities is open to objection.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle Râzî’nin nimeti ıtlâkı üzere “mâ lâbüdde minhü”den ta‘mîmi cây-i nazardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The main concern is the reproach-and-punishment question; by restricting that question to unbelievers, al-Razi effectively joins those who say the address is to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: asıl korkulacak mesele tevbih ve ikāb suâlidir, bunu ise Râzî kâfirlere hasretmiş olmakla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi’s distinction overlooks sinful believers: they may neglect obedience and be distracted by amusement and rivalry, so reproach must include them too.
rows.anchor: Fâsık mü’min olmakla beraber tâatsizlik etmiş, lehv ü tekâsüre kapılmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best reading follows al-Kashshaf and al-Baydawi: the question is for reproach and recompense, addressed to believers and unbelievers distracted by rivalry, and the definite article restricts the blessing to what distracts them.
rows.anchor: meseleyi Keşşâf’ın îzah ve Beyzâvî’nin telhis ettiği vechile bu âyette suâli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following surah’s exception for those who believe and do righteous deeds fully clarifies this interpretation.
rows.anchor: Nitekim bundan sonraki Asr Sûresi’ndeki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author renders the opening as ‘Did you not see how your Lord dealt with the people of the elephant?’
rows.anchor: Meâl: Görmedin mi, nasıl etti Rabbin ashâb-ı file?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to the Prophet; seeing is figurative for certainty of the heart, knowing as though one had seen with one’s eyes.
rows.anchor: Hitab Peygamber’edir. “Rü’yet” basariyeden istiare olarak rü’yet-i kalbiyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event was widely known through abundant eyewitnesses still alive, including people who had reached that time; the long-lived poet Labid is an example.
rows.anchor: o vakit onu gözleriyle gören şâhidleri henüz kesretle mevcud

rows.speaker: Âişe
rows.claim: Aisha reports having seen two elephant handlers left crippled and blind and begging in Mecca.
rows.anchor: Hatta “fili çekenlerden iki kişinin kötürüm, a‘mâ olarak kalıp Mekke’de dilendiklerini gördüm” diye Hazret-i Âişe’den rivayet dahi vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the address might be general to anyone who witnessed the event, the Prophet is the more apparent addressee because the event preceded his birth and he first received the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: mevlidine mukaddime olan âyât-ı ilâhiyeden olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ‘how did your Lord act’ asks about the manner of the act, not its bare nature, to draw attention to its marvel.
rows.anchor: “mâ-fe‘ale = ne yaptı?” diye fiilin mâhiyetinden değil, nasıl, ne keyfiyette yaptı diye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event’s extraordinary character lies in its manner: death and destruction are ordinary divine acts, but their unusual course here is miraculous.
rows.anchor: Çünkü bu istifham acâibliği ihtar içindir. Hâdisenin acîb, fevkalâde garib bir hârika olan ciheti de keyfiyetidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An analogy contrasts familiar human reproduction, which seems ordinary, with creating a human when none existed, which appears wondrous because experience has no regular precedent for it.
rows.anchor: bir insandan bir insan yaratmak haddizâtında pek büyük bir kudret ve sanat olduğu hâlde alışılmış bulunduğu için acîb görülmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The theologians call this the ‘aspect of proof’: merit lies in discerning such manners and their evidence, since overlooking subtle qualities prevents grasping the true value of things.
rows.anchor: Ki mütekellimîn buna “vech-i delil” tâbir etmişler ve medhe istihkak zevâtı görmekte değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the elephant are the famous army of Abraha, the Abyssinian governor of Yemen, who came with troops and elephants led by Mahmud to demolish the Kaaba but failed.
rows.anchor: Ebrehe ordusuna ki Yemen’i istîlâ etmiş Habeş valisi iken maiyyetindeki Habeş vesâireden mühim bir ordu ile Mahmud (Mamud) denilen fillerine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event gave the army its name and made that year a dating epoch among Arabs, who referred to events as occurring in, before, or after the Year of the Elephant.
rows.anchor: bu sene, Araplar beyninde عَامُ الْفِيلِ “Fil Yılı” diye mâruf olarak bir tarih mebde’i ittihaz olunmuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: According to the strongest report, Muhammad was born fifty days after the event in the Year of the Elephant.
rows.anchor: en sağlam rivayete göre Hazret-i Peygamber bu vak‘adan elli gün sonra doğmuştu.

rows.speaker: Nakkāş
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash, quoted through Rawḍ al-Unuf from Ibn Hisham’s biography commentary, dates the event to the first of Muharram in year 882 of Alexander’s era; this makes Muhammad fifty-two at the Hijra.
rows.anchor: Ravzu’l-ünüf’te “kıssa-i fil, İskender tarihinin sekiz yüz seksen ikinci senesi muharreminin evvelinde oldu” diye Nakkāş tefsirinden nakleder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author translates the verse as asking whether God submerged the enemy’s plans in utter loss.
rows.anchor: Kılmadı mı keydlerini tadlilde: fendlerini, düzenlerini tadlîle müstağrak kılmadı mı?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keyd is a concealed malicious design intended to harm another; because warfare also relies on such subtle schemes, the term can refer to war and fighting.
rows.anchor: diğerine bir mazarrat yapmak için gizli bir surette tedbir kurmaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turkish equivalents for keyd include düzen, fend, oyun, dolap, and tuzak.
rows.anchor: Lisânımızda “keyd”e “düzen”, “fend”, “oyun”, “dolap”, “tuzak” dahi tâbir ederiz.

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains dallala kaydahu as making the plot lost; al-Raʿd 13:14 uses dalal in the sense of loss or disappearance, and Imruʾ al-Qays was called Dalil for wasting his father’s estate.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf’ın beyan ettiği üzere ضَلَّلَ كَيْدَهُ denilir ki “dâll, zâyi‘kıldı” demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here tadlil means wholly losing, wasting, and nullifying the enemy’s designs, a stronger sense than merely confusing their plans.
rows.anchor: bütün bütün kaybettirip tamamen tazyî‘ile ibtal eylemek mânasını ifade eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction portrays every plan immersed in nullification; simply translating it as confusing their plans misses the more emphatic obliteration.
rows.anchor: bunda yalnız tedbîri şaşırtmaktan daha yüksek bir mâna bulunduğundan gaflet edilmemek gerektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question is confirmatory, effectively saying that God did this; the coordinated ‘and He sent’ follows from it.
rows.anchor: İstifham da takrîrî olduğundan “gördün a, kıldı” demektir. Ve ondan dolayı ma‘tûfunda وَأَرْسَلَ gelecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The army planned to destroy the Kaaba and replace it with the Kullays church it built in Sanʿa, redirecting pilgrims; at Mughammas, three farsakhs from Mecca, Mahmud would not advance, and the army was later destroyed.
rows.anchor: Tevâtüren mâlum olduğu üzere filleriyle gelip Kâbe’yi yıkmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author renders the birds as numerous swarms, coming in groups, flocks, and successive ranks.
rows.anchor: kuşlar ebâbîl alay alay, fırka fırka, bölük bölük birbiri ardınca katar katar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayr is the plural of tair, a flying bird; its indefinite form suggests unfamiliar, strange birds, reported as varied in size and black, green, or white.
rows.anchor: “Tayran” diye nekre olarak getirilmesi de bunların tanınmadık garib birtakım kuşlar olduğunu iş‘âr eder.

rows.speaker: Abdülmuttalib
rows.claim: The Prophet’s grandfather Abd al-Muttalib is reported to have described the birds as neither from Najd nor Tihama.
rows.anchor: Cedd-i nebevî Hazret-i Abdülmuttalib “ne Necdî ne de Tihâmî” demiş.

rows.speaker: Ferrâ
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says he had not heard an Arabic singular for ababil, which some treat as a plural without a singular like shamathit and abadid.
rows.anchor: Ferrâ “Arabdan müfredini işitmedim” demiş.

rows.speaker: Ebû Ubeyde Ma‘mer b. Müsennâ
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda likewise says he had seen no one claim that ababil has a singular.
rows.anchor: Ebû Ubeyde Ma‘mer b. Müsennâ da “bunun müfredi olduğunu söyleyen görmedim” demiş

rows.speaker: Abdullah b. Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: Ibn Masud glosses ababil as groups or flocks.
rows.anchor: Abdullah b. Mes‘ûd’dan firak

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the birds as following one another in succession.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan birbiri ardınca يـَتْبَعُ بـَعْضُهَا بـَعْضًا

rows.speaker: Abdullah b. Hâris b. Nevfel
rows.claim: Ibn Harith b. Nawfal compares the successive flocks to packed, grouped camels.
rows.anchor: Abdullah b. Hâris b. Nevfel’den ibil-i müebbele[^23] gibi ekātî‘, yani besi develeri gibi bölük bölük

rows.speaker: Sa‘îd b. Abdurrahman b. Ebzâ
rows.claim: Saʿid b. Abd al-Rahman b. Abza describes the birds as scattered or separate groups.
rows.anchor: Sa‘îd b. Abdurrahman b. Ebzâ’dan[^24] müteferrika

rows.speaker: Hasan ve Katâde
rows.claim: Hasan and Qatada interpret ababil as numerous birds.
rows.anchor: Hasan ve Katâde’den kesîre

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid describes them as varied groups, successive and assembled together.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den شَتَّى مُتَتَابِعَة مُجْتَمِعَة yani muhtelif ardı ardınca

rows.speaker: İbn Zeyd
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the birds came as varied groups from all sides.
rows.anchor: İbn Zeyd’den: şuradan buradan her taraftan gelmiş muhtelif

rows.speaker: İbn Cerîr
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir summarizes these glosses as scattered flocks arriving successively from different directions.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr bunları “müteferrik, birbiri ardınca muhtelif nevâhîden” diye hulâsa eylemiştir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Ca‘fer Revâsî
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar al-Ruʾasi says he heard ibbala as the singular of ababil.
rows.anchor: Ebû Ca‘fer Revâsî bunun müfredi olarak “ibbâle”yi işittiğini söylemiş

rows.speaker: Kisâî
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says he heard grammarians use ibbevl, while some used ibbil, as singular forms.
rows.anchor: Kisâî de nahviyyûnun “ibbevl” dediklerini, bazılarının da “ibbîl” dediklerini işittim demiştir.

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses ababil as groups and says its singular is ibbala, a large bundle; crowded flocks are likened to a great bundle, though it may also lack a singular like abadid and shamathit.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî “ebâbîl”, “hazâik” (yani cemaat) diye

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Al-Raghib compares ibbala to a bundle of wood and takes ababil as the plural of ibbil, meaning scattered groups like herds of camels.
rows.anchor: Râgıb da “‘ibbâle’ odun huzmesine teşbîhendir. ‘Ebâbîl’ ‘ibbîl’in cem‘idir.

rows.speaker: Kāmûs
rows.claim: The Qamus lists several possible singular forms and defines each as a flock or successive group of birds, horses, or camels; ibbala also means a bundle.
rows.anchor: Kāmûs’ta da şöyle diyor: “‘İbbâle’, ‘ibâle’, ‘ibbevl’

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether ababil has a singular or not, the author takes it to mean many birds arriving in numerous varied flocks, groups, and successive ranks.
rows.anchor: “Ebâbîl” bunlardan birinin cem‘i olduğu surette de mâna küme küme muhtelif bölükler hâlinde katar katar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author considers an additional possible implication of ‘bundle upon bundle’: calamity piled upon calamity, although no one is reported to have explicitly adopted this meaning.
rows.anchor: Fakat kimse bundan böyle bir mâna anladığını söylememiştir.

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some lexicographers and interpreters identify ababil as a known swallow-like mountain bird that cannot take off from the ground and nests high.
rows.anchor: bazıları “ebâbîl”in dağ kırlangıcı dedikleri bu kuş olduğuna zâhib olmuşlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports describe the birds as swallow-like and their palms as resembling dogs’ paws, which helped spread the species identification.
rows.anchor: Ekseriya bu kuşların vasfında أَمْثَال الْخَطَاطِيف “kırlangıçlar emsâli”, وَأَكُفُّهَا كَأَكُفِّ الْكِلاَبِ “avuçları kelb avuçları gibi”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects reading ababil as a species name: major exegetes explain it as a descriptor of varied, successive flocks, and the verse emphasizes their strangeness.
rows.anchor: Lâkin yukarıda görüldüğü üzere eimme-i müfessirîn “ebâbîl”in böyle bir nevi kuş ismi olduğunu söylememiş

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Although Ibn Abbas is reported to say they were swallow-sized with dog-like palms, the collected reports describe varied sizes and colors, not a single bird species.
rows.anchor: gerek hacim ve gerek renk itibariyle muhtelif olduğunu anlatmaktadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author pictures varied successive flocks from large carrion birds through crows to small insect-eating swallows, in black, white, green, and mixed colors, reportedly arriving from Yemen and the sea.
rows.anchor: türlü türlü ve birbiri ardınca tâkip ederek gelen muhtelif sürüleriyle irili ufaklı alay alay kuşlar demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author renders the birds as throwing stones of siccil at the people of the elephant.
rows.anchor: O kuşlar onlara, yani ashâb-ı file siccilden taşlarla atış ediyorlardı.

rows.speaker: Yûnus-ı Nahvî ve Ebû Ubeyde
rows.claim: Yunus al-Nahwi and Abu Ubayda tell Ibn Hisham that siccil in Arabic means very hard or solid.
rows.anchor: Yûnus-ı Nahvî ve Ebû Ubeyde bana şöyle ihbar ettiler: Siccîl, Arabın indinde şedîd sulb

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: A widely known interpretation transmitted from Ibn Abbas derives siccil from Persian seng-gil, stone and clay, yielding clay hardened like tile and the sense of hardness.
rows.anchor: Fi’l-vâki‘İbn Cerîr vesâire de İbn Abbas’tan mervî olduğu üzere en meşhur mânasında “siccîl” Farisî olan “seng, gil” muharrefidir.

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Al-Alusi reports a view deriving siccil from the Arabic sejl, a large bucket, with the stones pouring successively like water from a bucket.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî’nin beyânına göre bazıları bunun Arabî olan büyük kofa mânasına “secl”den olduğuna kāil olmuş

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats siccil as the register or record of the unbelievers’ punishment and derives it from sending, since punishment is described as sent in 105:3 and 7:133.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî der ki: “‘Siccîn’, küffarın amel defterlerinin adı olduğu gibi, ‘siccîl’ de azablarının yazıldığı divanın alemi gibidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the record interpretation, siccil denotes sent punishment; deriving it from the Arabic word for a register would fit better and make it a conventional religious term.
rows.anchor: Bu iki mânaca “siccîl” o taşların geldiği mahalli göstermiş olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports describe stones from lentil or chickpea size to hazelnut or sheep-dropping size; each bird carried three, and a strike pierced the victim through.
rows.anchor: her kuşun bir ağzında iki de ayaklarında olmak üzere üçer taşı hâmil bulunduğu

rows.speaker: Nevfel b. Ebû Muâviye ed-Dîlî
rows.claim: Nawfal reports seeing pea-sized, glass-like fragments larger than lentils, scratched like a Zafar bead.
rows.anchor: Ebû Nuaym’ın Nevfel b. Ebû Muâviye ed-Dîlî’den[^41] tahric ettiğine göre demiştir ki: “Ben ashâb-ı file atılan taşları gördüm

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Abu Nuaym’s report from Ibn Abbas gives the stones as hazelnut-sized.
rows.anchor: Ebû Nuaym’ın Delâil’de İbn Abbas’tan tahrîcinde fındık

rows.speaker: İbn Merdûye
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh’s report compares the stones to sheep droppings.
rows.anchor: İbn Merdûye’nin rivayetinde كَبـَعْرِ الْغَنَمِ koyun gübresi kadar.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: A report says Ibn Abbas saw a measure of these striped red stones at Umm Hani’s home, like Zafar beads.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf ve daha bazı tefsirlerde İbn Abbas’ın bunlardan birazını Ümmü Hânî’nin evinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports suggest the stones were hard, striped beads, illustrating the hardness sense of siccil.
rows.anchor: Bu taşların birer boncuk kadar sert ve çizgili olarak tehaccür etmiş olan salâbetini bir ifade vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse states no stone size; its indefinite wording suggests unfamiliar stones, siccil implies hardness or lethality, and the phrasing suggests they were witnessed.
rows.anchor: Âyette bu taşların hacimleri hakkında bir sarahat yoksa da “hicâraten” tenkîrinden gayr-i mâruf birtakım taşlar olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even ordinary hailstones can kill exposed people caught by surprise, so the extraordinary aerial barrage would devastate an exposed army.
rows.anchor: Böyle nohut ve fındık kadar bir dolu yağmuru bile açıkta ansızın yakaladığı insanları telef ettiği mâlumdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asf is a noun or verbal noun connected to bending, twisting, breaking, and scattering; exegetes offer several interpretations of crop foliage.
rows.anchor: “Asf” esasında eğip bükmek, kırıp dökmek mânalarına alâkadar olarak masdar ve isim olur bir kelimedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported glosses for asf include post-harvest leaves blown by wind and eaten by animals, broken straw, fresh leaves before the ear forms, and empty husks.
rows.anchor: Müfessirîn bunun ekin yaprağı demek olduğunu söyleyerek birkaç vecih zikretmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the basic sense of asf is green crop foliage, which dries and breaks into straw; green immature crop cut for fodder is also called asf.
rows.anchor: Kāmûs’ta da mezkur olduğu üzere “asf”ın asıl mânası بـَقْلُ الزَّرْعِ’dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turkish calls green crop cut before maturity hasıl or kasıl, so the author chooses hasıl for asf in the translation.
rows.anchor: Onun için biz de mealde “asf”ı “hasıl” diye terceme etmeyi muvâfık bulduk.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meʾkul means eaten, and the crop simile has three main readings.
rows.anchor: “Me’kûl” mâlum ki yenmiş, yenik demektir.

rows.speaker: Mukātil, Katâde ve Atâ
rows.claim: The first reading compares the army to crop eaten and trampled by animals, depicting its broken, scattered state; alternatively, the result implies dung and disintegrating corpses, expressed decorously by naming the crop before its eaten result.
rows.anchor: Mukātil’in, Katâde’nin, Atâ’nın kavilleri budur.

rows.speaker: İbn Cerîr ve Fahr-i Râzî
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir and Fakhr al-Razi prefer the first reading: eaten and trampled crop, or corpses reduced and scattered like dung by euphemism.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr ve Fahr-i Râzî gibi birçok müfessirîn bu vechi tercih eylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading also draws a decorous parallel with Qurʾān 5:75, where saying Jesus and his mother ate food euphemistically implies bodily relief.
rows.anchor: Nitekim كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ ٱلطَّعَامَ [el-Mâide 5/75] “Îsâ ve anası yemek yerlerdi” demek

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari appears to prefer the second, finer lexical reading: foliage eaten by worms or insects, leaving holes like the pierced bodies of the army before it could achieve its purpose.
rows.anchor: Bu, lügat itibariyle ince bir mâna demek olduğundan Zemahşerî bunu tercih etmişe benziyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading is foliage left as empty husks after the grains are eaten; ellipsis or figurative attribution would compare the bodies or burned insides to hollow grain-pods.
rows.anchor: Yine aynı mâna ile dâneleri yenmiş sade kapçıktan, samandan ibaret kalmış ekin yaprağı demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading comes most readily to mind, while asf and the Turkish hasıl both suggest foliage bent, broken, or cut while still fresh.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh zihne tebâdür eden mâna evvelki vecihtir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal and sequential fa in fa-jaʿalahum says the destruction followed the throwing of stones immediately and swiftly.
rows.anchor: فَجَعَلَهُمْ’deki فا sebebiyetle beraber ta‘kīb ifade ettiği için, taşların remyi üzerine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed the arrogant army quickly and extraordinarily, laying it low like crop already eaten; the army had trusted its elephants and numbers to destroy the Kaaba without opposition.
rows.anchor: Karşılarında zâhiren mukāvemet edecek bir kuvvet görmeyen, fillerine ve çokluklarına güvenerek istedikleri gibi Kâbe’yi yıkacaklarını zanneden müstevlî bir orduyu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event shows that God can inflict unimaginable calamities on comparable people at will, as with the mockers who are cast into the Hutama in the previous surah.
rows.anchor: evvelki sûrede geçtiği vechile hümeze lümeze gürûhunu da tutup hutameye fırlatıvereceğinde ne şüphe?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event was punishment for the army and a miraculous divine blessing and sign for Mecca, meant to teach its people a lesson.
rows.anchor: ashâb-ı fil hakkında ne kadar fecî ve hâil bir azab ve nikmet olmuşsa ehl-i Mekke hakkında da o nisbette ibret alınması lâzım gelen büyük ve hârikulâde bir nimet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not protect the then-idolatrous Meccans merely for their own sake or simply from care for the Kaaba; the event preceded Muhammad’s birth and his mission to purify the House and proclaim monotheism, as commanded in 22:26.
rows.anchor: yalnız Kâbe’ye olan i‘tinâ-yı ilâhîden dolayı da değil, وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِىَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْقَآئِمِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ [el-Hâc 22/26] emri vechile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular ‘your Lord’ rather than ‘your Lord’ plural signals special divine care for Muhammad; two surahs later this is summarized as the gift of al-Kawthar.
rows.anchor: sûrenin başında اَلَمْ تـَرَ كَيْفَ فـَعَلَ رَبُّكُم buyurulmamış, رَبُّكَ buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah honors the Prophet, gives believers glad tidings, warns unbelievers, and rebukes Quraysh for failing to value that divine favor.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle bu sûre Peygamber’e tekrim, mü’minlere bişaret, kâfirlere inzar ve bilhassa o nimetin kadrini bilmeyen Kureyş kâfirlerine imtinan ile itabdır.
